name: Name
body: LOT122923, from the personal effects of junior mechanik Anatoly Gerslev Ivadovich. Recovered from Black Dolfin Khardstadt, PROJECT NAME: VYGOR. Vitaly, My brother, I want you to know that I am safe, concerned as you must be with my unexpected absence. Agents of our empress arrived at my home in the early hours, and ordered me to accompany them. They were direct and treated me roughly during my removal, but since then, I have been well taken care of. I find myself in a large facility. From the dust and grime covering every surface, I believe this place has sat disused for some time. The snow outside the windows and atop the trees beyond the fence reassure me that I am still in our homeland, at least. We are not allowed to leave, but I do not lack for comforts—the vyatka in particular is from one of the finest distilleries in the empire. The soldiers here form a grim group. I suspect all of them are veterans of the Troubles. Among my companions, however, I have made friends. There are several other mechaniks here, some engineers, and a group of alchemists. There’s a large gymnasium where we can play futsal, a well-stocked library, and enough reign boards that none of us will be lacking. I have fond memories of you teaching me the game. I wonder if any of my new companions play, but have yet to ask.

name: Name
body: We may not know the reason we’ve been brought together, but there is a feeling amongst us. A sense of patriotism. I can’t say why, but I believe our work in this mysterious place will become a source of pride for our nation. With love from afar, Anatoly *** Vitaly, The number of people here has grown to hundreds! We must have a quarter of the whole Mechanik’s Assembly among us, to say nothing of the nation’s greatest engineers and arcane mechaniks. Our superiors have started organizing us into groups. The alchemists form one team, and the machinists another. Each day we face new challenges, each specific to our cabals’ specialties. Today’s task was a redesigned distribution header—a compact manifold with an improved separator and throttle assembly, designed to prevent wet steam from hammering the lines and keep pressure steady across the whole system. Whatever it is they have us working on, it appears it will require enough power to drive a colossal!

name: Name
body: With love from afar, Anatoly Vitaly, They have given us a schedule now. The facility has also been outfitted with proper clocks and bells, and clean lines have been painted on the floor for where we are to stand when a superior passes. The restoration is almost reassuring, in the way a familiar workshop’s chalk marks are reassuring. The tools we have been issued are under tight control; they are numbered, and we sign for them each morning as though we are borrowing our own hands. It leads to strange interactions. I asked for a set of micrometers—a simple instrument, far from a device that could be turned into a weapon. The quartermaster looked at me as if I’d requested a pistol. In the end, they provided what I asked for, but it arrived in a locked tin that must be returned at day’s end. I smile as I write this. It seems our empire fears precision. The food is good, even generous. They serve us meat often. Comfort staves off the grumbles and eases the tone when men talk. I am not the oldest here, but I am wise enough to notice how quickly a room full of experts with loud opinions can be turned into obedient children by warmth, drink, and routine.

name: Name
body: Do you remember the stove in father’s place? The one that always hissed because the vent was cut too narrow? I thought of it today when we argued over a steam header’s throat diameter. Hundreds of the finest minds in Khador are debating the same problem that makes a village stove spit. It should be funny. It is, in a way. Write to me if you can. Tell me something ordinary. Tell me the price of nails. Tell me the smell of the river. I find myself hungry for small truths and details. Your brother, Anatoly *** Vitaly, Today, the reason for our presence was revealed. A group of senior officials from High Kommand arrived from the capital to observe our progress on various projects, and to explain the significance of our work. They brought with them the warjack we are meant to restore—a machine I had only heard mention of by fellow KMA members and in nationalist papers. Behemoth. The warjack is in very poor condition, its various parts contained in several large crates. Sorting through their contents was like looking for a stone in the snow. Tons of shorn metal and damaged parts, all once of the highest quality but now scarred by the weapons and claws of the motherland’s enemies.

name: Name
body: The machine’s cortex was carefully packed away in a separate container. They opened it as if unveiling an icon, and for a moment, the whole room went quiet in a way I have only heard in cathedrals. When I tell you what I saw was the height of craftsmanship, please know it is only because I lack the poetic expression to fully capture the mastery in its construction. Every component and machined edge was of the highest quality. There were several pieces so advanced that even now, twenty years on from the warjack’s construction, I cannot fathom how they work or what function they serve. We have been told to build a body worthy of housing this vessel. Excitement and trepidation war within me in equal measure. Your brother, Anatoly *** Vitaly, This time, when they opened the container housing the cortex, I was close enough to smell it. Not oil, exactly. Old oil has a sweetness. This scent was sharper, a hot metal that has cooled too many times, the tang of insulation lacquer, a faint bite like burned coal dust trapped where it should not be. It is only the second time I have seen the cortex since its arrival, and still my breath catches to look upon it. I have never previously beheld a component which made proud engineers speak in hushed tones, but this instrument is beyond remarkable.

name: Name
body: We have built a temporary cradle to keep the cortex from shifting while the new chassis is fitted around it. The arcane mechaniks insisted on a suspension frame of laminated spring steel and shock bushings, so the housing doesn’t transmit vibration directly into the core. I argued for a simpler mount—I lost, but they were right. The instrument is too fine, and too exact. There are still components and marks on the casing that I do not understand, but I don’t know any of us do. We will no doubt learn their secrets in due course. Our superiors have begun assigning us in shifts that overlap oddly, as if they don’t want any one group alone with the instrument. Once I might have called that caution. If I am honest? Here it feels more like distrust. If my last letter sounded proud, it’s because I was. I still am. But pride is a thin blanket in a cold facility. With love from afar, Anatoly *** Vitaly, Although the soldiers assure us that our letters reach our families, I no longer trust their words. The glances they exchange when we hand over our letters seem too guilty, and the words in your replies do not sound like your own. From now on, I believe I write not to you, my brother, but to keep a record of these days of historic importance.

name: Name
body: Preliminary work on the chassis concluded last night. With its main platform constructed and cortex in place, one of our motherland’s warcasters has been assigned to assist us in familiarizing Behemoth with its new body, and to facilitate its communication with us. High Kommand has delivered a set of bombards to replace the original ones installed on Behemoth, and what tremendous weapons they are. These new cannons are considerably more destructive on the firing range than what we were testing before. When they conducted the first trial, I felt it through my teeth. This is not without its problems, however. The recoil impulse alone is enough to twist a brace if the load path isn’t perfect, and their kinetic force can topple the warjack with its current configuration. Some are suggesting a total redesign and complete chassis rebuild will be necessary, and I fear I agree. To think that anyone in the empire would consider this Behemoth too small! Anatoly ***

name: Name
body: To the clerk who reads this, good evening. I hope you like the talk of mechaniks. We have test-fired the weapons again. I expected them to be more potent than before, but firing both weapons simultaneously felt like a foolish dare instead of a test, shaking loose bolts we had peened and re-peened. It was not just recoil—it was a kind of contempt for anything not built like a fortress. We are working to resolve the problem in three ways. Mount geometry: we are widening the trunnion stance, lowering the centerline, and trying to keep the recoil from turning into a lever that pries the chassis apart. Energy management: we have installed counter-recoil pistons and spring stacks within the main chassis—not elegant, but nothing about this is elegant anymore. Load path reinforcement: we have installed ribs, gussets, and an internal lattice of bracing that, if you squint, looks like cathedral buttresses. I have never seen brilliant people reduced to arguing over where a force "wants to go." It wants to go everywhere, my friend. That is the problem.

name: Name
body: A soldier made a joke today: "If it can’t stand the kick, it doesn’t deserve the gun." Everyone laughed... yet the mirth did not reach their eyes. Anatoly *** To the apparatchik assigned to pry into my correspondence, The arcane mechaniks have delivered on their promise of a new generation of sub-cortexes. The new instruments generate gunnery solutions fast enough that the loaders can barely keep pace. On the test range, they hit a target moving as fast as a galloping destrier. There was no need to launch a second barrage. We have been tasked with producing shoulder armor to properly shield these new sub-cortexes from cannon fire and explosive impacts. I have proposed a series of shock absorbers to mitigate internal effects within the housing and provide additional protection, similar to the cradle we constructed to hold the primary cortex. Anatoly *** Should even I bother addressing these letters anymore, now I have stopped receiving replies from my "brother"? The pretense is over and I would rather not be wasteful with the ink. Still, I wonder, does High Kommand enjoy my words, or should I be more deferential in the future?

name: Name
body: Perhaps a reply will be forthcoming. Perhaps not. My team leader proposes that a series of lower limbs, similar to those on Cryxian submersible warjacks, would provide a more even distribution of forces and help the Behemoth remain stable. With the assistance of the machinists, we shall have a prototype ready for testing later today. Update: the multiple-leg pattern was a complete failure. The force of the bombards is far in excess of what the design can effectively support. Five soldiers were injured when the limbs sheared from the chassis and were flung across the testing field. The machine pulled itself along the ground toward us before our warcaster could rein it in. It was like Behemoth blamed us for the failure and wanted to mete out punishment. Anatoly *** Another attempt, and yet another failure. Father used to say, "Failure is a new opportunity to learn". He was right, but I am tired, and hungry for some semblance of success. The recoil of these weapons is beyond enormous. We thought reinforcing the joints by another seven inches would be enough to protect them during firing, but they cracked after a second volley. You might think we mechanics are the most disappointed in this failure, but I suspect the machine itself is even more frustrated than we are.

name: Name
body: Anatoly *** There were whispers among our unit this morning. There are four fewer arcane mechaniks than yesterday. Most think the missing men tried to flee the facility and return to their families. I do not know what I think—but last night, I heard baying hounds outside the fence perimeter. I doubt we will see the missing men again. What do you think, Mr. Apparatchik? Did the veterans of the Troubles add a few more Khadoran lives to their tallies last night? Is even asking this the signature of my own death warrant? *** After many days of effort, failures, and frustration, we are at last close to a breakthrough. A new Winter Korp detachment has been assigned to our garrison, and among them is a heavily armored vehicle that we believe holds the salvation of our purpose. They are like war wagons, but powered by a boiler and furnace akin to the workings of a steamship. Instead of wheels, they use flexible linkages to better distribute the vehicle's weight. The team leaders have consulted with our overseers, and are requisitioning several of these "Bisons" for further experimentation.

name: Name
body: *** Today, we trialed our first Bison-footed configuration. The tracked conveyance showed promising results in the force-to-ground-contact ratio, but further improvements are needed before additional testing. The alchemists have provided us with a new alloy, which they claim can help to lower the center of mass for the entire configuration. *** Vitaly, We stand on the cusp of achieving our goals. Tomorrow, Behemoth shall undergo its final testing. I do not expect anything but exemplary results. I am not alone. Yet, in this moment of triumph, I realize that this development has condemned me. All of us here know the inner workings of this new Behemoth intimately. All the challenges we have overcome are the seeds of vulnerabilities that an enemy could exploit. I shall not walk out of this place. None of us will. If I am truthful with myself, I have always known that even my earliest letters would never have reached you. Writing to you has been the carrot the empire has used against me, knowing the stick would always follow it, and I embraced this hollow gesture all the same. I did not speak up, nor resist.

name: Name
body: That I was somehow complicit in this deception provides scant consolation as I lay in my bunk, unable to sleep. I miss you, my brother. Anatoly *** We have succeeded. Behemoth has excelled in every test. A steam plant fit for a warship is housed within the body of the railless machine that will carry Behemoth into battle. The warjack’s advanced sub-cortexes not only calculate the trajectories of its destructive volleys, but are now also connected to gyroscopic stabilizers. The stabilizers make constant corrections to the link tension, idler alignment, and tread timing, so the body remains level even when the guns try to shove it sideways. There is nothing more to do than admire our work. Our kingdom’s most significant weapon has been transformed into something transcendent, a machine that will define future generations of warfare. I wish I could watch as Behemoth races across the battlefield toward our enemies, awe-inspiring as it unleashes its mighty barrages. No target on our range has been able to withstand a full volley from it, nor shall the motherland’s foes.

name: Name
body: It seems completion of our work could not have been more timely—I suspect that something has changed in the world outside this complex. Another set of guards assigned to watch us have been redeployed, replaced this time by fresh-faced recruits. The High Kommand no longer visits us to hear progress reports. The people who claim to have an ear to the outside world… they look afraid of something. Something significant. Something that could threaten all of us. Threaten Khador. Still, I am not concerned. The motherland has asked me to make a sacrifice, so that she shall live. The pride of the empire has been returned to service, and Khador shall triumph in even the darkest of days ahead. Isn’t that worth everything? Vitaly, I pray that it was. Your brother, Anatoly >>High Kommand recommendation: Retain Anatoly Gerslev’s writings for posterity as classified military records. Deliver a letter to his next of kin informing them of his heroic service to the Motherland and award Anatoly Gerslev the Shield of Khardovic (posthumous).<<
